heroHeadline: ICC Prosecutor Seeks Warrants for Smotrich, Ben-Gvir, and Three Others; IDF Kills Hamas Armed Wing Chief al-Haddad in Rimal Airstrike
heroSubtitle: The International Criminal Court's prosecutor applied on May 17, 2026 for sealed arrest warrants for Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, Settlements Minister Orit Strock, and two senior IDF officials — dramatically expanding the ICC's legal campaign against Israel's political and military leadership, following the November 2024 warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant and the May 13 rejection of Israel's jurisdictional challenge. On May 15, IDF airstrikes on the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad — Hamas's armed wing commander in Gaza and one of the last surviving architects of October 7 — along with 6 others and wounded 50+; Hamas confirmed his death on May 16 as IDF continued strikes on Rimal residential buildings. Separately, tens of thousands marched in London on May 16 (11 arrests) in pro-Palestinian demonstrations following the 78th Nakba anniversary. UN human rights experts demanded on May 17 the immediate release of detained Gaza-bound flotilla activists, citing torture allegations. UN OCHA reported 45 Palestinian structures demolished in the West Bank in just one week (May 5–11), 90% used for agriculture or water access. The Gaza death toll stands at 72,619+ since October 7, 2023, with ~900+ killed since the October 2025 ceasefire amid a deadlocked Hamas disarmament standoff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
